name: Revvi
description: REVVI - ENTITY PROFILE FOR NEWS SOURCING Prepared 27 July 2026. All figures third-party unless marked official.  ================================================================ 1. CORE IDENTITY ================================================================  Brand name: Revvi (also styled REVVI).   Trades primarily as a brand; confirm the registered legal entity at   Companies House before wiring up any filings feed.  Website: revvi.co.uk  What it does: Designs and supplies children's electric balance bikes   and electric motorbikes - battery-powered, throttle-driven,   off-road-styled two-wheelers for riders roughly aged 2 to early teens.  Founded: 2015, out of a motorbike and dirt bike background. Stated   objective is to design and supply affordable, high-quality electric   motorbikes and balance bikes for children as an entry point into the   sport.  Base: Chobham, Surrey, United Kingdom.  Scale and funding: Tracxn lists Revvi as unfunded with approximately   five employees as of January 2025 - a small, apparently bootstrapped   operation rather than a VC-backed one. Directional only; this is   third-party data, not filed accounts.  Positioning claim: Markets itself as the UK's number one kids'   electric bike brand. Retailers describe it as the UK's leading brand   for kids' electric balance bikes.  Sector labels:   Short caption      - Kids' Electric Bikes   Descriptive        - Electric Balance Bikes for Kids   Industry framing   - Consumer Discretionary / Leisure Products                        (youth electric micromobility)  ================================================================ 2. PRODUCT RANGE ================================================================  Model names follow wheel size. Current and announced lineup:   12", 16", 16" Plus, 16" XL, 18", 20", 20" Plus, 24"  Defining product characteristics:   - Freewheel system allows the bike to be ridden as a conventional     unpowered balance bike; a twist throttle then adds power.   - Selectable, parent-lockable speed modes so children progress at     their own pace.   - No gears, no clutch - twist-and-go simplicity.   - Removable batteries, swappable in around 20 seconds.   - Lightweight: the entry 12" model weighs 9kg, with slow (5mph) and     fast (10mph) modes.   - Near-silent operation versus petrol equivalents - a recurring     marketing point (garden/backyard riding).   - Adjustable handlebars that raise in increments as the rider grows.  2026 LAUNCHES - the live news story:   Revvi 24"     - First Revvi built to carry riders into their teens.     - 1500W peak power; 48V 15Ah battery.     - Three selectable modes: 15.5, 22 and 30mph.     - Hydraulic disc brakes, full suspension, 24" wheels.     - Dealer pre-orders opened with a UK launch around May/June 2026;       first batch limited and allocated in pre-order sequence.   Revvi 20" Plus     - Upgrades the best-selling 20" platform with the same 48V motor,       adjustable suspension and hydraulic brakes.     - Expected late August 2026; first batches limited.  ================================================================ 3. DISTRIBUTION MODEL ================================================================  Supplies bikes and products across the UK and Ireland via a dealer network plus its own direct-to-consumer website.  Implication for the collector: a large share of Revvi "news" surfaces through dealers and retailers rather than the company itself. Dealer blogs often break spec and launch detail before mainstream trade press, but they are commercial content and should be weighted lower for credibility and sentiment.  Named dealers and retailers publishing Revvi content:   Judd Racing (describes itself as Revvi's largest dealer)   Skates.co.uk   Future Riders   Offspring MX   Go Off Road Barnsley   Garland Powersports   Motocross4U   Revolve Moto   AW Cycles   Torbay Motocross   Claudy Cycles   Scoot n Skates   Davant Bikes  ================================================================ 4. COMMUNITY AND EVENTS - THE REVVI CUP ================================================================  Revvi anchors a branded youth racing series, the Revvi Cup, run in partnership with EXGB (Electric X GB); Paul Oughton runs the events.    - Classes have expanded alongside new models so riders from age     three upwards can take part.   - Sits alongside a British Indoor EX Championship and the Electric     Dirt Bike Festival at Greenfield Dirt Track, Lincolnshire.   - Continues into 2026 - e.g. a round at Apple Valley, June 2026.   - Dirt Hub maintains a dedicated Revvi Cup news feed carrying race     reports and results.   - Revvi's own site promotes limited edition colours and Revvi Cup     events to its mailing list.  Note: event coverage will dominate raw article volume. If the newsroom is meant to surface commercially meaningful news, race results should sit in a separate, deprioritised bucket.  ================================================================ 5. COMPETITIVE SET ================================================================  Direct competitors (2026):   STACYC  - strongest premium brand recognition in the category   Amped   - increasingly popular, value-led   Oset   Kuberg   Torrot  Caution: Tracxn's algorithmic competitor list names Maeving, Zapp and Mission Electric. These are adult electric motorcycle brands and are a poor comparator. Do not let a data provider seed the peer set.  ================================================================ 6. REGULATORY AND RISK CONTEXT TO MONITOR ================================================================    - Not road-legal. Like all kids' electric bikes, Revvis are for     private land use. Any UK regulatory movement on off-road electric     two-wheelers, private land use, or youth e-mobility is directly     relevant.   - Lithium battery safety, product recalls, and toy/product safety     standards (UKCA/CE) are the standing tail risks for the category.   - Import tariffs, shipping costs and Chinese manufacturing exposure     - likely relevant given the price positioning, though the     manufacturing location is unconfirmed.   - Category-level demand: discretionary children's spend, sensitive     to consumer confidence and seasonal (Christmas, spring/summer)     peaks.  ================================================================ 7. SEARCH CONFIGURATION ================================================================  PRIMARY QUERY TERMS   Revvi   Revvi bikes   Revvi electric bike   Revvi balance bike   Revvi Cup   Revvi 24   Revvi 20 Plus  CONTEXT ANCHORS (require at least one, to cut noise)   electric balance bike   kids electric bike   e-balance bike   dirt bike   motocross   youth electric   Chobham   EXGB  NEGATIVE KEYWORDS - critical. "Revvi" is a short invented word that collides badly:   Revvity        - NYSE-listed life sciences company (formerly                    PerkinElmer). High-volume financial news; will                    flood any loose match.   Revvi Card     - US subprime credit card brand. Different company.   Revolt Motors  - Indian electric motorcycle maker; surfaces                    repeatedly on Revvi searches.   Revv / Revel / Rev / "revving" / "rev up" - generic motoring                    language.    Suggested exclusions:     Revvity, PerkinElmer, credit card, Revolt Motors, India, NYSE  PREFERRED SOURCES, RANKED   1. revvi.co.uk (official - new models, range pages, dealer news)   2. Revvi Instagram and Facebook (launches and Revvi Cup appear here      first)   3. exgb.co.uk and dirthub.co.uk (event and series coverage)   4. UK cycling / powersports trade press - BikeBiz, Dirt Bike Rider,      MoreBikes   5. Companies House (accounts, officers, charges)   6. Dealer blogs (fast on specs, commercially motivated)  LOW-SIGNAL PATTERNS TO SUPPRESS   - Product listing and stock-availability pages   - "How to build" guides and buying guides   - Review roundups containing no new information   - Boilerplate origin text. The paragraph beginning "Revvi was     founded in 2015. As a company we have a huge passion for     motorbikes and dirt bikes..." is copy-pasted verbatim across     dozens of dealer sites and will generate constant duplicate hits.     Use it as a canonical string to dedupe against.  ================================================================ 8. NEWS ANGLES WORTH FLAGGING ================================================================  High value:   - New model launches, pre-order openings, delivery slippage   - Dealer network changes; international or export expansion   - Funding, acquisition, or ownership change   - Companies House filings: accounts, new officers, charges   - Product recalls or safety notices   - Regulatory change affecting off-road youth electric bikes   - Competitor moves (STACYC, Amped) that reprice the category  Medium value:   - Awards, trade show appearances, brand partnerships   - Substantive independent reviews of new models  Low value / deprioritise:   - Revvi Cup round results and race reports   - Dealer promotional posts and stock notices
